- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially 1.00) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment was bullish in prior 3–5 days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00–0.33) — add 2–5% to forecast if recent sentiment is low or trending down.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot — adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead by subtracting 1–3% from peak predictions if recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at +5% above 7-day moving average for first 7 days.
- Sentiment 0.67–0.33 zones: forecast should be closer to 7-day average than to 30-day average — use 7-day average as anchor for mid-term forecasts.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is 0.67 and price is rising, don’t assume continuation — add 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is inconsistent or fading.
